source_text: Εἰ γὰρ καὶ τὰ τῆς χάριτος ἴσα ὑμῖν καὶ τοῖς ἐν τῇ τελευτῇ μυσταγωγουμένοις, ἀλλὰ τὰ τῆς προαιρέσεως οὐκ ἴσα, οὐδὲ τὰ τῆς παρασκευῆς τῶν πραγμάτων. Ἐκεῖνοι μὲν γὰρ ἐν τῇ κλίνῃ λαμβάνουσιν, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἐν τοῖς κόλποις τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τῆς κοινῆς ἁπάντων ἡμῶν μητρός· κἀκεῖνοι μὲν ὀδυρόμενοι καὶ δακρύοντες, ὑμεῖς δὲ χαίροντες καὶ εὐφραινόμενοι· ἐκεῖνοι στένοντες, ὑμεῖς δὲ εὐχαριστοῦντες· κἀκεῖνοι μὲν πολλῷ κεκαρωμένοι τῷ πυρετῷ, ὑμεῖς δὲ πολλῆς ἐμπεπλησμένοι τῆς πνευματικῆς ἡδονῆς. Ὅθεν ἐνταῦθα μὲν ἅπαντα σύμφωνα τῇ δωρεᾷ, ἐκεῖ δὲ πάντα ἐναντία τῇ δωρεᾷ· καὶ γὰρ θρῆνος καὶ ὀδυρμὸς πολὺς μυσταγωγουμένων, καὶ παιδία περιίσταται κλαίοντα, καὶ γυνὴ τὰς παρειὰς καταξαίνουσα, καὶ φίλοι κατηφεῖς, καὶ οἰκέται δακρύων γέμοντες, ὅλον τὸ τῆς οἰκίας σχῆμα χειμερινήν τινα καὶ ζοφώδη μιμεῖται ἡμέραν· ἐὰν δὲ αὐτὴν τοῦ κατακειμένου τὴν καρδίαν ἀναπτύξῃς, σκυθρωποτέραν τούτων εὑρήσεις. Καθάπερ γὰρ ἄνεμοι μετὰ πολλῆς τῆς ῥύμης ἐξεναντίας ἀλλήλοις ἐμβάλλοντες εἰς πολλὰ τὸ πέλαγος διατέμνουσι μέρη· οὕτω καὶ οἱ λογισμοὶ τῶν τότε κατεχόντων δεινῶν εἰς τὴν τοῦ κάμνοντος ἐμπίπτοντες ψυχὴν, εἰς πολλὰς τὴν ἐκείνου διάνοιαν σχίζουσι φροντίδας. Ὅταν εἰς τὰ παιδία ἀπίδῃ, τὴν ὀρφανίαν αὐτῶν ἐννοεῖ· ὅταν πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα ἀποβλέψῃ, τὴν χηρείαν λογίζεται· ὅταν ἴδῃ τοὺς οἰκέτας, τὴν ἐρημίαν ἁπάσης σκοπεῖ τῆς οἰκίας· ὅταν πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐπανέλθῃ, τῆς παρούσης ἑαυτὸν ἀναμιμνήσκει ζωῆς, καὶ ἀποῤῥήγνυσθαι μέλλων, πολὺ δέχεται τῆς ἀθυμίας τὸ νέφος. Τοιαύτη ἡ τοῦ μέλλοντος μυσταγωγεῖσθαι ψυχή. Εἶτα μεταξὺ τῶν θορύβων καὶ τῆς ταραχῆς αὐτῆς, ἐπεισέρχεται ὁ ἱερεὺς αὐτοῦ τοῦ πυρετοῦ φοβερώτερος ὢν, καὶ τοῦ θανάτου τοῖς τοῦ κάμνοντος προσήκουσιν ἀπηνέστερος· τῆς γὰρ τοῦ ἰατροῦ φωνῆς τῆς ἀπογινωσκούσης τὴν ζωὴν τὴν ἐκείνου μείζων ἀπόγνωσις εἶναι νομίζεται ἡ τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου εἴσοδος, καὶ θανάτου σύμβολον εἶναι δοκεῖ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ἡ ὑπόθεσις. Ἀλλ' οὔπω τὸν κολοφῶνα ἐπέθηκα τῶν κακῶν· μεταξὺ γὰρ θορυβούντων τῶν ἐπιτηδείων καὶ παρασκευα49.225 ζομένων, παλλάκις ἔρημον ἀφεῖσα τὸ σῶμα ἀπεπήδησεν ἡ ψυχὴ, πολλοὺς δὲ καὶ παροῦσα οὐδὲν ὤνησεν. Ὅταν γὰρ μήτε τοὺς παρόντας ἐπιγινώσκῃ, μήτε φωνῆς ἀκούῃ, μήτε ἀποκρίνασθαι δύνηται τὰ ῥήματα ἐκεῖνα, δι' ὧν τὴν μακαρίαν συνθήκην πρὸς τὸν κοινὸν ἡμῶν ἁπάντων καταθήσεται Δεσπότην, ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ξύλον ἀργὸν ἢ λίθος, ὁ φωτίζεσθαι μέλλων πρόκειται νεκροῦ μηδὲν διαφέρων, τί τῆς μυσταγωγίας ὄφελος ἐν ἀναισθησίᾳ τοσαύτῃ; βʹ. Τὸν γὰρ τοῖς ἱεροῖς τούτοις καὶ φρικτοῖς μέλλοντα προσιέναι μυστηρίοις ἐγρηγορέναι χρὴ καὶ διεγηγέρθαι, πάσης βιωτικῆς φροντίδος εἶναι καθαρὸν, πολλῆς γέμειν σωφροσύνης, πολλῆς προθυμίας, πάντα τὸν μυστηρίων ἀλλότριον λογισμὸν ἐξορίζειν τῆς διανοίας, καὶ πάντοθεν καθαρὸν παρασκευάζειν τὸν οἶκον, ὥσπερ αὐτὸν ὑποδέχεσθαι μέλλοντα τὸν βασιλέα. Τοιαύτη τῆς ὑμετέρας διανοίας ἡ παρασκευὴ, τοιοῦτοι παρ' ὑμῖν οἱ λογισμοὶ, τοιαύτη τῆς ψυχῆς ἡ προαίρεσις. Τὴν μὲν οὖν ἀξίαν ἀμοιβὴν τῆς ἀρίστης ταύτης γνώμης ἀναμένετε παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ ταῖς ἀντιδόσεσι νικῶντος τοὺς τὴν ὑπακοὴν ἐπιδεικνυμένους τὴν πρὸς αὐτόν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ χρὴ καὶ τοῖς συνδούλοις τὰ παρ' ἑαυτῶν εἰσενεγκεῖν, καὶ τὰ παρ' ἡμῶν εἰσοίσομεν, μᾶλλον δὲ οὐδὲ ταῦτα ἡμέτερα, ἀλλὰ καὶ ταῦτα Δεσποτικά.
thought_title: Deathbed baptism is no match for deliberate preparation
orientation: Chrysostom is still addressing the catechumens, contrasting their deliberate preparation with those baptized at the last breath.
pass_a_gloss: For even if the things of grace are equal for you and for those being initiated at the end, yet the things of choice are not equal, nor the things of preparation of affairs. For those receive on the bed, but you in the bosom of the Church, the common mother of us all; and those lamenting and weeping, but you rejoicing and being glad; those groaning, but you giving thanks; and those weighed down by much fever, but you filled with much spiritual pleasure. Wherefore here all things are in harmony with the gift, but there all things are opposed to the gift; for both lamentation and much wailing of those being initiated, and little children stand around weeping, and a wife tearing her cheeks, and friends downcast, and household slaves full of tears, the whole appearance of the house imitates a wintry and gloomy day; and if you open the heart of the one lying down, you will find it more sullen than these things. For just as winds with much force rushing against one another cut the sea into many parts, so also the thoughts of the evils then holding fast, falling into the soul of the one who is sick, split his mind into many cares. When he looks at the children, he thinks of their orphanhood; when he looks toward the wife, he reckons the widowhood; when he sees the household slaves, he considers the desolation of the whole house; when he returns to himself, he reminds himself of the present life, and being about to be torn away, he receives a great cloud of despondency. Such is the soul of the one about to be initiated. Then in the midst of the tumults and its disturbance, the priest enters, being more fearful than the fever itself, and harsher to the relatives of the sick man than death; for the entrance of the elder is thought to be a greater despair than the voice of the physician giving up his life, and the undertaking of eternal life seems a symbol of death. But I have not yet put the capstone on the evils; for in the midst of the friends making a disturbance and making preparations, often the soul, leaving the body deserted, has leaped away, and even being present it benefited many nothing. For when he neither recognizes those present, nor hears a voice, nor is able to answer those words through which he will make the blessed covenant with the common Master of us all, but like a useless log or stone, the one about to be baptized lies there differing nothing from a corpse, what is the profit of the initiation in such insensibility? 2. For the one about to approach these sacred and awesome rites must be awake and roused, be clean of every worldly care, be full of much self-control, much eagerness, banish every thought alien to the rites from the mind, and prepare the house clean on every side, as if about to receive the king himself. Such is the preparation of your mind, such are the thoughts among you, such is the choice of the soul. Therefore await the worthy recompense of this best judgment from God, who in his repayments surpasses those who display obedience toward him. But since it is necessary also to contribute to fellow servants the things from ourselves, we will also contribute the things from us; rather, not even these are ours, but these too are the Master's.

choices.english: in the bosom of the Church
choices.why: Literal rendering of κόλποις as 'bosom' preserves the maternal image Chrysostom immediately develops with 'common mother of us all'.
rejected: in the embrace of the Church
in the lap of the Church

choices.why: καρόω means to be stupefied or heavy-headed; 'weighed down' captures the oppressive physical state while keeping the passive participle.
καταξαίνω is a strong verb meaning to lacerate or rend; 'tearing' conveys the violent grief gesture literally.

choices.term: χειμερινήν τινα καὶ ζοφώδη μιμεῖται ἡμέραν
choices.english: imitates a wintry and gloomy day
choices.why: Literal rendering of μιμεῖται as 'imitates' keeps the theatrical metaphor of the house's appearance.
rejected: resembles a wintry and gloomy day
takes on the look of a wintry and gloomy day

choices.english: being about to be torn away
choices.why: ἀπορρήγνυμι means to break or tear off; the passive infinitive with μέλλων conveys the imminent violent separation from life.

choices.english: I have not yet put the capstone on the evils
choices.why: κολοφών is literally the summit or finishing touch; 'capstone' preserves the architectural metaphor of completing a list of evils.
rejected: I have not yet reached the peak of the evils
I have not yet added the crowning evil

pass_b_english: For even if the gifts of grace are equal for you and for those who are initiated at the end of life, the gifts of deliberate purpose are not equal, nor are the gifts of preparation for the realities. Those receive baptism in their bed, but you receive it in the bosom of the Church, the common mother of us all. Those are weeping and shedding tears, but you are rejoicing and celebrating. Those are groaning, but you are giving thanks. Those are weighed down by much fever, but you are filled with much spiritual pleasure. Therefore here everything is in harmony with the gift, but there everything is opposed to the gift. For there is much lamentation and wailing of those being initiated, and children stand around crying, and a wife tears her cheeks, and friends are downcast, and servants are full of tears. The whole appearance of the house imitates a wintry and gloomy day. And if you open up the heart of the one lying there, you will find it more sullen than these things. For just as winds rushing against each other with great force cut the sea into many parts, so the thoughts of the terrible things that then hold sway fall upon the soul of the sick person and split his mind into many cares. When he looks at his children, he thinks of their orphanhood. When he turns his eyes to his wife, he reckons her widowhood. When he sees his servants, he considers the desolation of the whole house. When he returns to himself, he remembers his present life, and being about to be torn away, he receives a great cloud of despondency. Such is the soul of the one about to be initiated. Then, in the midst of the confusion and its disturbance, the priest enters, more frightening than the fever itself and harsher than death to the sick person's relatives. For the entrance of the priest is considered a greater despair than the voice of the physician who gives up hope for his life, and the very subject of eternal life seems a symbol of death. But I have not yet put the capstone on the evils. For in the midst of the confusion of friends and their preparations, the soul often leaves the body behind and leaps away, and even when present it benefited many people not at all. For when the one about to be baptized does not recognize those present, nor hears a voice, nor is able to answer those words through which he will make the blessed covenant with the common Master of us all, but lies there like a useless log or stone, differing nothing from a corpse, what is the benefit of initiation in such insensibility?

For the one about to approach these sacred and awesome rites must be awake and alert, must be clean of every worldly care, must be full of much self-control and much eagerness, must banish from his mind every thought foreign to the sacred rites, and must prepare the house clean on every side, as if he were about to receive the King himself. Such is the preparation of your mind, such are the thoughts among you, such is the deliberate purpose of your soul. Therefore await the worthy recompense of this excellent resolve from God, who surpasses with his rewards those who show obedience to him. But since we must also contribute what is ours to our fellow servants, we will contribute what is from us—or rather, not even these things are ours, but these too belong to the Master.
notes: The source contains 'παρασκευα49.225 ζομένων' with a page number '49.225' embedded mid-word; this is a digitization artifact from the printed edition and the word should be read as 'παρασκευαζομένων' (making preparations).

problems.source_quote: θανάτου σύμβολον εἶναι δοκεῖ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ἡ ὑπόθεσις
problems.why: ὑπόθεσις here means 'proposal/introduction' (of the topic of eternal life), not 'undertaking'; the syntax is reversed—it's 'the introduction of eternal life seems a symbol of death'.
problems.fix: the introduction of eternal life seems a symbol of death
problems.ruling: ὑπόθεσις means 'proposal/introduction'; 'undertaking' misleads; syntax: 'the introduction of eternal life seems a symbol of death.'
